messages:
Ash K: FYI - apac-gpu pool autoscaler allowed a ~2.4x burst yesterday afternoon, ended up ~1.2K GPU-hours over our baseline forecast. We also saw 8 node evictions in eu-west tied to transient network flaps which amplified autoscaler churn. Need tighter guardrails before the holiday promo. Thoughts on a dual-threshold model (steady vs burst credits) + faster decay for burst credits?

Maria L: Can you paste the raw query numbers? Is the excess from prefix-cache misses or new cold starts?

Ash K: Query I ran: `SELECT sum(gpu_hours) FROM usage WHERE pool='apac-gpu' AND ts >= now()-72h` -> extra ~1,200 GPU-hrs vs moving baseline. Breakdown: ~78% short-chat traffic, cache hit rate dropped ~18% after the model rollback at 2026-03-12 09:00 UTC.

Jake P: Proposed approach: maintain a small "reservoir" of burst credits per pool (e.g., 200 GPU-hr/day) + a hard cap relative to baseline (hard_cap_multiplier=3). Also tighten scale-up smoothing to 60s. Need to check p99 latency impact though.

Lucy S: Oncall logs show the evictions around 14:12 UTC - `dmesg` had repeated network disconnects. Autoscaler saw transient control-plane CPU pressure and spun up replacements; replacements came up while evicted nodes were still terminating -> overshoot. We should add a cooldown and a node-creation rate limit to avoid compounding events.

Dave R: Cost math: 1.2K GPU-hrs * $2.10/hr ~= $2,520. If the promo triples burst events we could be looking at +3.5K GPU-hrs/week (~$7.3k/wk). We should be able to throttle burst budget for non-critical traffic to control spend.

Maria L: @Ash K please draft a config suggestion and a short canary plan. I'll run sims against the past 7 days once we have config.

Ash K: Draft config suggestion (rough):
```
burst_budget: 200 # GPU-hrs/day per pool
burst_credit_replenish_window: 24h
burst_decay_half_life: 3h
steady_target_util: 65%
hard_cap_multiplier: 3
scale_up_cooldown: 60s
node_creation_rate_limit: 2/hour
```
This implies autoscaler changes + small UI surface in Console to show remaining burst credit.

Jake P: Ran a quick sim locally with historic traffic. With burst_budget=200 we reduced overshoot by ~48% but saw a +0.8% bump to p99 in the worst-case scenario. Tradeoff looks reasonable for user-facing chat (we keep latency SLOs mostly intact).

Lucy S: :thumbsup: Agree on node_creation_rate_limit. Also add a fallback path: when burst credits exhausted, route to a smaller model variant with <100ms added latency to avoid spinning up new nodes. That reduces cost and churn.

Ash K: Plan: open PR with autoscaler config change + canary rollout to `apac-gpu-small` for 48h. Canary metrics to watch: gpu-hours delta, node churn, p99 latency, error rate, cache hit rate. @Maria L @Jake P please review sims and the canary dashboard when I post the PR.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout scheduled -> autoscaler-config/dual-threshold -> apac-gpu-small @ 2026-03-18T15:00Z

Maria L: I'll run sims and post results by EOD. Also recommend a temporary per-account throttle for holiday promo users if the canary flags too much overspend.

Ash K: Thanks all. If sim numbers look good we'll proceed with canary and a short-lived promo quota. I'll open the runbook and include rollback steps + a quick query set for SRE to run during the canary.

Lucy S: One more ops note - add an alert for "node-creation-rate > configured limit" so we can catch misconfig regressions quickly.

Dave R: And add a cost-alert for exceeding daily burst_budget spend by 20% so finance can triage promo spend ASAP.
